_: An estimated 4,000-7,000 polar bears live in Alaska and on the surrounding sea ice. The population is known to be in decline.
Russia is home to an estimated 3,000 polar bears, which live around Chukotka, Northern European Russia, and Siberia
Canada has an estimated 16,000 polar bears, spread across Labrador, Manitoba, Newfoundland, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Ontario, Quebec, and Yukon Territory.
Approximately 270 polar bears live within the boundaries of the Svalbard archipelago itself and an additional population of 700+ live on the sea ice north of Svalbard.
Greenland's polar bear population is unclear, but could include 7,000+ polar bears, spread among west Greenland, southeast Greenland, the Davis Strait, and the Kane Basin.
